title: Given a string, return the longest contiguous substring that reads the same forwards and backwards.
shortTitle: Longest Palindromic Substring — expand around center

s1_definition.profdef: Expand-around-center technique: every palindrome has a center, either a single character (odd length) or a gap between two characters (even length). For each of the 2n−1 centers, expand outward while the characters match and track the longest span. Time O(n²), space O(1).
s1_definition.analogy: A reference-code checker at National Bank of India looks for the longest mirror-symmetric stretch inside a code. It stands at each possible middle point and grows outward in both directions as long as the two sides keep matching, remembering the widest mirror it finds.
s1_definition.oneliner: Try every center, expand while both sides match, keep the longest span.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Expand-around-center technique: every palindrome has a center, either a single character (odd length) or a gap between two characters (even length). For each of the 2n−1 centers, expand outward while the characters match and track the longest span. Time O(n²), space O(1).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** A reference-code checker at National Bank of India looks for the longest mirror-symmetric stretch inside a code. It stands at each possible middle point and grows outward in both directions as long as the two sides keep matching, remembering the widest mirror it finds.

**One line to remember:** Try every center, expand while both sides match, keep the longest span.

sections.s2_technical:
There are 2n−1 possible centers: n single-character centers for odd-length palindromes and n−1 between-character centers for even-length palindromes. For each center, expand with two pointers moving outward while they stay in bounds and the characters are equal, then record the span if it beats the best. For example: `while (l >= 0 && r < s.length() && s.charAt(l) == s.charAt(r)) { l--; r++; }`.

After the loop, the valid palindrome is from l+1 to r−1 because the loop overshoots by one on each side. You call the expansion once with the center as (i, i) for odd length and once as (i, i+1) for even length, and keep the maximum.

The time is O(n²) because each of the roughly 2n centers can expand up to O(n), and space is O(1). A senior nuance is that Manacher's algorithm solves this in O(n) by reusing mirror information, but expand-around-center is the expected interview answer for its simplicity and constant space.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At National Bank of India, a validator scans reference codes for the longest mirror-symmetric stretch, since certain legacy codes embed palindromic checksums. This is exactly how Longest Palindromic Substring works.

Problem 2 — Palindromes can be odd or even in length, so a single center model misses half the cases. This is exactly why both single-character and between-character centers are expanded.

The mini-project builds a `PalindromeFinder`, a `BankLogFormatter`, and a runnable demo.

sections.s5_journey:
The input string is babad.

Step 1: At center index one, the character b, odd expansion grows to b-a-b because the a and b mirror, giving length three.

Step 2: The even expansion at each gap finds no matching pair of equal adjacent characters here.

Step 3: Other odd centers like index two also find three-length palindromes such as aba.

Step 4: The longest span stays at three, so start and end bound bab.

Step 5: The result is bab, and for cbbd the even center between the two b characters gives bb.

```text
2026-10-27T03:20:00Z [INFO] National Bank of India — Palindrome Finder (Longest Substring)
2026-10-27T03:20:00Z [INFO] Longest palindrome = bab
2026-10-27T03:20:00Z [INFO] babad → bab
2026-10-27T03:20:00Z [INFO] Longest palindrome = bb
2026-10-27T03:20:00Z [INFO] cbbd → bb
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```text
  s = b a b a d
  center i=1 (odd):  expand b|a b a → "bab" len 3
  center gap (even): no equal adjacent pair extends
  best span = [0,2] → "bab"
  2n-1 centers ; expand while s[l]==s[r] ; span = r-l-1
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Longest Palindromic Substring is best solved with the expand-around-center technique. The key insight is that every palindrome has a center, which is either a single character for odd-length palindromes or the gap between two characters for even-length palindromes, so there are about two times n minus one centers to try.

For each center I expand two pointers outward as long as they stay in bounds and the characters on both sides match, then I record the span if it beats the longest found so far. Because the expansion overshoots by one on each side when it stops, the actual palindrome length is the right pointer minus the left pointer minus one. I run the expansion once treating the center as a single character and once as a gap between two characters, and keep the maximum.

In my project at National Bank of India, a validator scanned reference codes for the longest mirror-symmetric stretch, because some legacy codes embedded palindromic checksums. I used expand-around-center for its simplicity and constant space, and I mention that Manacher's algorithm can do it in linear time by reusing mirror information when the input is very large.
